Subject: Follow-up: Long-document fit & next steps for HeklaHealth

Hi Maya / Liam —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

What we heard
- Primary use case: clinical note summarization + structured extraction from long patient histories (range: single notes ~3–8k tokens; multi-note bundles up to ~60k tokens).
- Key non-negotiables: preserve factual details (med list, dates), low hallucination rate for medication/events, and stable summarization fidelity across long inputs.
- Volume: pilot = ~20k docs (sanitized subset), production could be 100k+/mo later.

Risks and signals to measure
- Truncation risk for >32k token batches (their ingestion varies). We should measure where prefix/context gets dropped vs. model-style summarizer behavior.
- Summarization fidelity: abstraction vs. extractive balance — short summaries must not drop critical items (meds/conditions).

Proposed evaluation approach (short)
1) Red team quick check: run 20 sanitized docs through two model families we usually recommend for long-context: a 16k-optimized dense model and a 70B quantized variant for extreme-long runs.
2) Metrics: truncation rate, ROUGE-L on reference summaries, targeted extraction accuracy for key fields, and a small human-review pass (30 samples).
3) Operational tests: measure p95 latency for 4k/16k/32k/64k prefixes, and token cost delta with and without prefix/KV caching.

Initial model candidates (we will refine after sample):
- redwood-sentry-16k (balanced for contextual fidelity + latency)
- redwood-llama-70b-q4 (for robust long-tail fidelity at higher cost)

Requested from you
- Please share the sanitized sample (20 documents) you mentioned so we can run the first pass. If you prefer, SFTP or a Drive link is fine.
- Confirm which fields are must-have in the summaries (e.g., meds, allergies, next steps).

Artifacts I attached for the evaluation kickoff:
- hekla_sample_index.jsonl (stub) — metadata index we can use to track documents
- longdoc_prompt_set_v1.txt (stub) — initial prompt templates and anchors for extractive checks

Next steps
- We’ll run an initial pass within 72 hours of receiving samples and send back a short scoreboard + example outputs.
- If results look good, propose a 2-week pilot with a 1k-doc canary and a post-pilot quality review.

Thanks — paging Rishi and Marcus for model/ops notes below.

Best,

Thanks — running a quick operational + model plan from infra/ML side. High level recommendations: 

Model shortlist and rationale:
- redwood-sentry-16k: good latency/cost balance for 8–16k windows and strong extractive behavior with prompt anchors.
- redwood-recall-64k-alpha: experimental long-window (64k) for multi-note bundles — will surface truncation characteristics, but expect higher memory pressure.
- redwood-llama-70b-q4: higher-fidelity headroom if extraction fidelity is below threshold on smaller models.

Evaluation matrix (we will implement):
- Automated: truncation_rate (percent tokens dropped), token_efficiency (tokens per useful summary token), ROUGE-L vs reference, extraction recall/precision for meds/dates.
- Human: 30-sample blind recall test for critical fields + timeline ordering score.

Ops notes:
- We'll use prefix/KV caching on repeated patient histories to reduce repeated compute. That will materially reduce cost for multi-note bundles — expect ~25–40% token cost reduction in typical reuse patterns.
- For the 64k runs, we'll evaluate two runtime configs: tiled attention (if available on infra) vs. chunked summarization (overlap + stitch). Each has different hallucination/ordering tradeoffs.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Day 0 (on sample receipt): run 20-doc pass with redwood-sentry-16k + redwood-recall-64k-alpha and return scoreboard + 10 example outputs.
- Day 3: human-review pass + recommended canary config.
- Day 7: full pilot proposal + estimated token costs and latency SLOs.

I've added a short plan into our shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=long-window-eval-plan-hekla (private link). Also attached the evaluation checklist.
